title: 2027 Toyota Prius Plug-In Hybrid Pricing, Specs, and Release Date
summary: The 2027 Toyota Prius Plug-In Hybrid continues as one of the most affordable plug-in models available. Changes include a new exterior colo and blacked-out Nightshade trim level.
body_markdown:
The Toyota Prius Plug-In Hybrid debuted for the 2017 model year, although it was then known as Prius Prime. The new name was introduced in 2025 and, as it suggests, this is a plug-in hybrid (PHEV) version of the regular Prius hybrid, which we review separately. The Plug-in Hybrid version looks identical apart from its badging and added charging port. It also gains 26 horsepower over the standard Prius.

## What’s New for the 2027 Toyota Prius Plug-In Hybrid


For 2027, the Toyota Prius Plug-In Hybrid carries over unchanged except for a new Nightshade trim level that mirrors the features of the Nightshade Edition available during the 2026 model year. It adds blacked-out styling elements for about $800 more on top of the mid-tier XSE trim level. There’s also a new Inked exterior color available across all trim levels.


## Design


The Toyota Prius Plug-In Hybrid shares the same small and sleek hatchback body as the regular Prius. The Prius Plug-In Hybrid features 17-inch wheels and is available with 19-inch wheels. The Nightshade trim level, which slots just below the top XSE Premium, comes with black exterior trim and black 19-inch wheels.


## Powertrain


The Toyota Prius Plug-In Hybrid features the same 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine from the regular Prius plus two electric motors, a 13.6-kWh lithium-ion battery pack, and a continuously variable transmission (CVT). It’s rated for 220 hp, which is 26 hp more than the front-wheel drive version of the regular Prius. That said, the regular Prius is available with all-wheel drive (AWD) and the plug-in hybrid version is not. The Prius Plug-In Hybrid has peppy acceleration and a well-tuned suspension system that results in a surprisingly enjoyable driving experience. Even better, it’s rated for up to 52 mpg combined in base trim, and up to 44 miles of electric range on a full charge.


## Interior


The Toyota Prius Plug-In Hybrid is a snug hatchback with seating for five, though we wouldn’t advise squeezing three adults in the second row. The front row is reasonably comfortable, but this is one of the smallest four-door cars currently on sale, and there’s no mistaking it for anything else. That said, there’s a surprising amount of cargo space, with 20.3 cubic feet behind the second row and 26.7 cubic feet with the second row folded down. Manually adjustable front seats, cloth upholstery, and a heated steering wheel come standard. Options include a power liftgate, heated front seats, heated rear seats, power-adjustable front seats, synthetic leather upholstery, and a panoramic roof.


## Technology


The Prius Plug-In Hybrid comes with a 7-inch digital instrument display, an 8-inch touchscreen display, and a six-speaker audio system. Wireless Android Auto and Apple CarPlay come standard and the infotainment system is intuitive and user-friendly. There are also easy-to-use physical controls for the climate control system. Toyota offers a 12.3-inch touchscreen, wireless charging, a digital key, and an eight-speaker JBL stereo.

## Safety


The Prius Plug-In Hybrid features a competitive safety package, with features such as a rear-view camera, adaptive cruise control with low-speed and traffic-jam capability, front collision warning, pedestrian detection, automatic emergency braking, blind-spot monitors, lane-departure warnings, lane-keep assist, safe-exit assist, a rear-seat alert system, and front and rear cross-traffic alert. The 2027 Toyota Prius Plug-In Hybrid has not yet been crash-tested by the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) or the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), but the 2026 model earned top Good scores in its two IIHS crash tests.


## Pricing and Release Date


The 2027 Toyota Prius Plug-In Hybrid is on sale now and, at the time of writing, pricing started at $33,980 for the SE model. The XSE starts at $37,230, while the Nightshade starts at $38,000 and the top-spec Limited starts at $40,675. These prices do not include Toyota’s destination fee of $1,295.
